claim: Residential property is assessed at 9.5% of market value; taxable value is a percent of fair market value, 9.5% for all other property, 11.5% for industrial.
An assessment appeal is filed with the county assessor no later than 30 days after the date of the assessment schedule notice, stating why the assessment is incorrect.
The county board of equalization hears the appeal and may affirm the assessor's valuation or find for the taxpayer and remand; written findings are due by October 1 each year.
A taxpayer may appeal a county board of equalization decision to the State Board of Equalization within 30 days of entry of the decision or its legal postmark mailing date, whichever is later.
The appeal must address market value, not the tax rate, and must include evidence supporting the owner's estimate of market value.
An order of the State Board of Equalization may be appealed to the district court of the county where the property is located.
An action to enjoin an illegal assessment, levy or collection must be filed in district court within one year following the illegal assessment, levy or collection.
Every Wyoming resident is entitled to a homestead not exceeding $100,000 in value, exempt from execution and attachment for debts (creditor-protection exemption).
The homestead is exempt only while occupied by the owner or the owner's family; when two or more persons jointly own and occupy a residence, each is entitled to the exemption.
A homestead may be a house on a lot or lands of any number of acres, or a house trailer or other movable home.
The creditor-protection homestead exemption does not apply against attachment or execution for the purchase money of the property.

A conveyance or mortgage of a homestead must contain words releasing homestead rights and be signed and acknowledged by the owner and the owner's spouse (not required for a conveyance directly from husband to wife).
Property tax Homeowner's Exemption removes 25% of the taxable value of an owner-occupied single-family dwelling and associated improved land, on the first $1,000,000 of fair market value.

claim: Long-term Homeowner's Exemption removes 50% of fair market value up to $3,000,000 for owners age 65 or older (or with a spouse 65 or older) who have paid Wyoming residential property taxes for at least 25 years; the years need not be consecutive.

A sworn statement by the grantee or agent disclosing parties, transfer date, legal description and the actual full amount paid must accompany a deed presented for recording; the clerk may not record without it.
The sworn sale-price statement is not a public record and is confidential, used by assessors and the Department of Revenue only for sales-price ratio statistics.

The price statement may omit price and terms for transfers including foreclosure or delinquent-tax sales, gifts of over half the value, and spouse-to-spouse or parent-child transfers for nominal consideration.

Wyoming mortgages containing a power of sale may be foreclosed by advertisement within 10 years after maturity of the debt or recording.

Prerequisites include default, no pending suit on the debt, the mortgage and assignments recorded, and written notice of intent to foreclose sent by certified mail to the record owner and person in possession at least 10 days before publication begins.

Notice of sale is published for four consecutive weeks, at least once each week, in a newspaper in the county; a copy is also served by certified mail on the owner, occupant and subordinate lienholders at least 25 days before the sale.
The sale is at public auction between 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. at the courthouse door, conducted by the person named in the mortgage or the sheriff, to the highest bidder.
Owner may redeem within three months from the date of sale by paying the purchase price plus 10% annual interest and taxes or prior liens paid by the purchaser.
For agricultural real estate (over 80 acres outside a city or subdivision, or used substantially for agriculture), the redemption period is 12 months.
Surplus sale proceeds go to the mortgagor on demand after costs, the foreclosed debt and junior liens; the mortgagor is liable for any deficiency.
A foreclosure sale may be postponed by publishing notice of postponement for two consecutive weeks in the newspaper that carried the original advertisement.

Lands sold on execution or decree of foreclosure must be sold at public auction between 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the same day.
The time and place of the sale must be advertised for four consecutive weeks in a legal newspaper of general circulation in the county.
The foreclosing party or its authorized agent must be present or must have waived in advance the right to appear and bid; the sheriff is not considered the foreclosing party's agent.
Redemption is allowed within three months of the sale (12 months for agricultural real estate) at the bid price plus 10% annual interest; the sheriff issues a certificate of redemption.
If the owner does not redeem, judgment creditors and mortgagees or lienholders may redeem within 30 days after the owner's redemption period expires.
Foreclosure costs include the officer's sale fee, not to exceed $10, and advertising, and are paid from sale proceeds.

A distributee may file for summary distribution of real or personal property, including mineral interests, if the entire estate does not exceed $400,000 less liens and encumbrances, no earlier than 30 days after death.
The summary distribution application must attach a sworn report of value for Wyoming real property, which may be based on a broker's price opinion by a person with no interest in the estate.
Notice of the summary distribution application is published once a week for two consecutive weeks and mailed to the spouse and other distributees within 10 days after first publication.
The small-estate affidavit for payment of debts or delivery of personal property requires 30 days since death, no pending personal representative appointment, and an estate not exceeding $400,000.
A personal representative is entitled to possession of all real and personal estate of the decedent until settlement or court-ordered delivery to the heirs.
Title to a decedent's property passes to devisees or heirs but is subject to the personal representative's possession and court control for administration and sale, and to payment of debts.
Surviving spouse or minor children are entitled to the decedent's homestead; if no survivor, the homestead is liable for the decedent's debts.

Extra charges: $1.00 per additional name beyond five grantors/grantees of a different surname, and $1.00 per section, block, lot or tract description in excess of ten.
An unrecorded conveyance is void against a later good-faith purchaser for value whose conveyance is recorded first.
A recorded instrument gives notice to and takes precedence over later purchasers from the time of delivery to the county clerk for record.
A county clerk may receive, index and store electronic documents and accept fees electronically, and must continue to accept paper documents.
An electronic document and electronic signature satisfy legal requirements for originals, writing, signature and notarization as a condition of recording.

A deed of quitclaim and release is sufficient to pass all the estate the grantor could lawfully convey by a deed of bargain and sale.
The statutory short-form quitclaim deed names the grantor, consideration, grantee, description and county, and 'conveys and quitclaims ... all interest' in the property.
A quitclaim deed in the statutory form conveys the grantor's existing legal and equitable rights but does not extend to after-acquired title unless words are added expressing that intent.
A quitclaim without the word 'release' is still sufficient to pass all the estate the grantor could convey.
A deed or mortgage of a homestead must contain a release of homestead rights and be signed and acknowledged by the owner and the owner's spouse.
Taxes on real property are a perpetual lien on the property against all persons except the United States and the State of Wyoming.
Property taxes: 50% due September 1 and payable on and after November 10; 50% due March 1 and payable on and after May 10; no interest if paid in full by December 31.
Delinquent property taxes bear interest at 18% per year until paid.
A holder of a certificate of purchase or tax deed has a lien superior to all other liens except junior tax sales or later tax payments, enforceable in district court like a mortgage foreclosure.
In such a lien foreclosure the property is sold by the sheriff without appraisal, no deficiency judgment may be rendered, and any interested person may redeem before court confirmation.
The state tax lien filing fee with the county clerk is $20.00; release is included in the filing fee.
The county treasurer advertises a real property tax sale once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, first publication at least four weeks before the sale.
Sales are held at the county courthouse between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.; the person offering to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is the purchaser and receives a certificate of purchase.
Property not sold for the amount due is bid in for the county.
After four years from the date of sale the treasurer issues a tax deed to the county for unredeemed certificates, after at least 60 days' notice to the assessed owner and mortgagees.
A certificate holder may apply for a tax deed not less than four nor more than six years from the original sale, with proof of notice served at least three months before application.

Forcible entry and detainer may be brought against tenants holding over or three days after failure to pay rent, and against occupants after foreclosure or power-of-sale sales when the purchaser demands possession.
The party must give notice to leave at least three days before commencing the action.
The summons is served not less than three nor more than twelve days before the trial date set by the judge.
The defendant is not required to file a written answer to participate fully in the trial.
No continuance longer than two days is granted to the defendant unless a bond for rent and costs is given.
If the renter does not vacate under a court order, the sheriff may remove the renter's possessions and prevent reentry.
After regaining possession, valuable abandoned property requires written notice giving seven days to reclaim.
The holder of the owner's interest in a residential rental unit at termination of the rental agreement is bound by the deposit-notice and deposit-return provisions of W.S. 1-21-1207 and 1-21-1208.
A purchaser at a foreclosure or power-of-sale sale may use forcible entry and detainer once possession is demanded.
Tenants holding over their terms may be removed by forcible entry and detainer; the notice to leave is at least three days.
